_readme: This file is the signature -> repo/verb map for scripts/triage.py, the act-loop that
replaced per-message LLM triage in #alerts. A 'signature' is `source:external_id`
from ~/.hermes/watchdog.db's `events` table (source = one of slack_alert, uk,
docker_homelab, docker_vps, hermes_log, op_refs_homelab, op_refs_vps).
MATCH TARGETS (this is the part that was missing in the first draft of this file):
`rules`/`ignore` are matched against TWO candidate strings per event, in order, first
match wins across BOTH: `source:external_id` (the raw form) and
`source:normalize_title(title)` (the human-readable form, same normalize_title() as
scripts/watchdog-poll.py). For a grouped source (slack_alert, hermes_log) these are
usually the SAME string, since that source's external_id already IS
normalize_title(title) — see aggregate_slack_batch()/poll_hermes_logs(). For a state
source (uk, docker_homelab, docker_vps, op_refs_*) they differ: uk's external_id is an
opaque, unglobbable UptimeKuma monitor id ('204'), so `uk:macmini-dev-host-push` (the
title-derived target) is what makes that source mappable at all — a rule written
against the numeric id would break the moment the monitor is recreated.
Matching is glob-style (Python fnmatch: `*`, `?`, `[seq]`). `rules` matched
top-to-bottom, first match wins. `ignore` is checked FIRST, before everything else — a
match sends the item straight to state `ignored`: never carded, never escalated, never
even in the digest. Use `ignore` ONLY for a genuine recovery or a known-benign pattern
you have looked at and decided is truly nothing — see `ignoreUnstructuredSlackProse`
below for the very different case of 'this looks like it might matter but isn't
structured enough to auto-route'. No rule match at all -> the item stays unmapped
(state `new`, never escalates, carried silently) and its signature shows up in the
once-a-day digest so this file can grow deliberately instead of silently missing real
problems.
`ignoreUnstructuredSlackProse` (bool) is a STRUCTURAL filter, not a glob list, checked
AFTER `ignore`: any `slack_alert` item whose title does not start with a recognized
bot-alert shape (`[`, the siren emoji, checkmark, warning, or a bold-mrkdwn warning) is
routed to STATE_NOTE — NOT `ignored`. This distinction is load-bearing: `ignored` is
terminal AND invisible, and this DB genuinely contains rows like a human-written 'the
1Password rate-limit root cause is X, the two-line fix is Y' diagnosis that was never
shipped — dropping that into `ignored` would recreate the exact failure this whole
redesign exists to kill. STATE_NOTE is ALSO terminal (never escalates, never gets its
own card) but IS surfaced, once a day, under its own heading in the digest, so a real
diagnosis stays visible instead of vanishing. WHY THE FILTER EXISTS AT ALL: before
#alerts was silenced (see config.yaml), Hermes replied in that channel to every
message, and watchdog-poll.py's slack_alert poller ingested those replies right
alongside real bot alerts — hundreds of German/English sentences ('Alles grün.
„:ok_hand:“') sitting in `events` as if they were alert signatures. Silencing the
channel stops NEW ones; this flag is what keeps the existing backlog visible-but-quiet
instead of either flooding the channel with cards or disappearing into `ignored`.
`verb` is the other rule outcome, instead of `repo`: routes to a declared, code-side
ALLOWLISTED local command (VERB_ALLOWLIST in scripts/triage.py) rather than a sideclaw
episode — this file names a KEY ('env-check'), never a command; the argv is decided in
code, on purpose, so a policy edit alone can never run something arbitrary. Terminal
state for a verb outcome is `needs_human`, with the command's own output inlined on
the card. Used for op_refs_homelab/op_refs_vps: a dead 1Password ref is a deterministic,
already-diagnosed condition (hermes-ops.sh's env-check already returns the dangling
item name) — dispatching an episode to 're-discover' it would be slower AND worse: a
bare item name in a dispatched verdict can collide with sideclaw's own
`op://vault/item/field` secret-scan pattern and get withheld, whereas env-check's output
reaching the card directly does not.
Every `repo` value MUST resolve under `root` in config/dispatch-repos.json and MUST
NOT appear in that file's `deny` list — scripts/triage.py checks the deny list
itself before ever shelling out, so a rule naming a denied repo just silently never
escalates (logged to stderr) rather than crashing, but it is still a bug in this
file, not a feature. `homelab-private` is denied and 'shelfmark' below is why it is
in `ignore` rather than mapped to it: shelfmark is a third-party image
(ghcr.io/calibrain/shelfmark) running in the private compose file — nothing to
dispatch an investigation against even if the repo were reachable.
THE CONVENTION FOR WHICH REPO OWNS AN INFRA-SIGNAL ALERT (this is the part a real VPS
outage trace caught wrong once already — the argo rules below used to point at `argo`):
an infra-signal alert about a RollHook-managed app maps to the repo that owns its
COMPOSE FILE AND DEPLOY TARGET, not the repo that owns its source. `argo` is
compose-managed manually inside `vps` (`apps/argo/compose.yml`, `make argo-up` —
nothing in argo's own repo redeploys it), so a downed argo container maps to `vps`.
Most OTHER vps-hosted apps in this policy (audio-gateway, research-gateway, meteo,
image-gen, image-share) are the opposite: dispatch-repos.json's own comment documents
that they deploy to the VPS on every push to THEIR OWN repo's master (GitHub Actions ->
RollHook), so a code fix in their own repo auto-redeploys — mapping those to their own
repo is correct and deliberate, not an oversight to 'fix' the same way. Before adding a
new vps-app rule, check `vps/apps/<name>/compose.yml` AND whether that app's own repo
has its own deploy workflow before deciding which direction the rule should point. The
HyperDX-origin alerts (job.reaped, podcast.failed, vps-edge-*, ...) map to `vps` for a
related but distinct reason: their threshold/definition lives in
vps/observability/alerts/*.json, which is where THAT fix lands regardless of which
service the alert is about.
To extend: run
sqlite3 ~/.hermes/watchdog.db "SELECT source, external_id, title FROM events
WHERE resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY first_seen DESC LIMIT 40;"
and add a rule (or an ignore pattern) for anything real that shows up unmapped —
remembering a `uk` rule almost always wants the title-derived target, e.g.
`uk:some-monitor-name-push`, never the bare numeric id.
